proposals.before: He became friends across the generations with two eminent Sui veterans — Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Cui Zujun, Attendant Gentleman of the Household — and through them won a name for himself.
proposals.after: He became friends across the generations with two eminent Sui veterans — Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of the Capital Inspectors, and Cui Zujun, Imperial Diarist — and through them won a name for himself.
proposals.reason: 司隸大夫 is the Sui capital-inspector title, not 開府儀同三司; 起居舍人 is the imperial diarist, not Attendant Gentleman of the Household.

proposals.before: The Sui officials Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Cui Zujun, Attendant Gentleman of the Household, were both veteran ministers of great standing; they became friends despite the age gap, and thereby he gained renown.
proposals.after: The Sui officials Xue Daoheng, Grand Master of the Capital Inspectors, and Cui Zujun, Imperial Diarist, were both veteran ministers of great standing; they became friends despite the age gap, and thereby he gained renown.
proposals.reason: Same office mistranslations of 司隸大夫 and 起居舍人 as in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: After Husizheng defected to Goguryeo, Shilian was punished for their association and demoted to registrar at Zhuyuan in Annam. His mother was too old to endure the southern climes, so he left his wife Xianyu to tend her and set out alone.
proposals.after: After Husizheng defected to Goguryeo, Shilian was punished for their association and demoted to registrar at Zhuyuan. His mother was too old to endure the southern miasmas, so he left his wife Xianyu to tend her and set out alone.
proposals.reason: Chinese names 硃鳶 only; Annam is an invented geographic gloss not in the source sentence.

proposals.before: In time he asked to retire. He was released from the vice directorship but given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag, made co-equal with the three departments at third rank, and kept in charge of state affairs.
proposals.after: In time he asked to retire. He was released from the vice directorship but given the dignity of opening an office with ceremonial equality to the Three Ministers, made a third-rank colleague of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and kept in charge of state affairs.
proposals.reason: 開府儀同三司 is not Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag; 同中書門下三品 is third rank with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

proposals.before: After a long while he requested retirement; he was permitted to resign the vice directorship and was given Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag, Co-equal with the Three Departments, Third Rank, and charge of state affairs.
proposals.after: After a long while he requested retirement; he was permitted to resign the vice directorship and was given the dignity of opening an office with ceremonial equality to the Three Ministers, third rank equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery, and charge of state affairs.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 開府儀同三司 as a Golden Bag honorific.

proposals.before: He demoted the Cui to third rank and had the register published empire-wide.
proposals.after: He then placed Cui Gan as the third surname and had the register published empire-wide.
proposals.reason: Chinese names 崔幹; the idiomatic English drops the personal name and treats the demotion as the Cui clan only.

proposals.before: An edict also barred intermarriage among the seven great surnames in ten houses: the Li of Longxi, Wang of Taiyuan, Zheng of Xingyang, three branches of the Lu of Fanyang, two branches of the Cui of Qinghe, the Cui of Boling, and the Li of Zhao.
proposals.after: An edict also barred intermarriage among the seven surnames and ten houses: Li Bao of Longxi under Later Wei, Wang Qiong of Taiyuan, Zheng Wen of Xingyang, Lu Ziqian, Lu Ze, and Lu Fu of Fanyang, Cui Zongbo and Cui Yuansun of Qinghe, Cui Yi of Boling under Former Yan, and Li Kai of Zhao under Jin.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names ten ancestral individuals with dynastic labels; the idiomatic abridgment keeps only clan seats and omits the personal names.

proposals.before: Thereafter declining clans dropped from the registers, those not admitted in the line of descent all called themselves "forbidden-marriage houses," prized themselves all the more, and men and women secretly betrothed one another; the Son of Heaven could not forbid it — the age regarded it as a abuse.
proposals.after: Thereafter declining clans dropped from the registers, those not admitted in the line of descent all called themselves "forbidden-marriage houses," prized themselves all the more, and men and women secretly betrothed one another; the Son of Heaven could not forbid it — the age regarded it as an abuse.
proposals.reason: English article error: "a abuse" should be "an abuse."

proposals.before: He was promoted to grand master of ceremonies for the crown prince.
proposals.after: He was promoted to supervisor of the household of the crown prince.
proposals.reason: 太子詹事 is the household supervisor of the heir apparent, not the grand master of ceremonies (太常).

proposals.before: He was promoted to Grand Master of Ceremonies for the Crown Prince.
proposals.after: He was promoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Crown Prince.
proposals.reason: 太子詹事 is misrendered as Grand Master of Ceremonies.

proposals.before: Whenever policy was debated he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor grew still closer, once brought him into his private quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillar states — your house and mine were among them.
proposals.after: Whenever policy was debated he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor grew still closer, once brought him into his private quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillars of state — your house and mine were among them.
proposals.reason: 八柱國 are the Eight Pillars of State, not pillar states.

proposals.before: Whenever political gains and losses were discussed he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor drew closer to him, once brought him into the inner sleeping quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillar states — your house and mine were among them.
proposals.after: Whenever political gains and losses were discussed he cited antiquity as instruction; the emperor drew closer to him, once brought him into the inner sleeping quarters, and said, "In antiquity Zhou had eight pillars of state — your house and mine were among them.
proposals.reason: Same 八柱國 mistranslation as pillar states.

proposals.before: Later, summoned to court, he was granted a seat in the imperial tower but sat without proper decorum; when again seated to receive an imperial message, the emperor in anger said, "When you went to Shu you all but wiped out the twenty mounted guards I gave you — my own Longzhong cavalry escort would scarcely be enough for you."
proposals.after: Later, summoned to court, he was granted a seat in the imperial tower but sat without proper decorum; when again seated to receive an imperial message, the emperor in anger said, "When you went to Shu you all but wiped out the twenty mounted guards I gave you — my own Long-stock cavalry escort would scarcely be enough for you."
proposals.reason: 隴種 refers to men of Longxi stock, not a place named Longzhong.

proposals.before: Later he entered court; granted a seat in the imperial tower, his bearing was not respectful; again seated facing the edict, the Emperor angrily said: "When you entered Shu, the twenty mounted attendants of my carriage and fast-steed escorts — you executed nearly all of them; my Longzhong cavalry escort still would not suffice for you."
proposals.after: Later he entered court; granted a seat in the imperial tower, his bearing was not respectful; again seated facing the edict, the Emperor angrily said: "When you entered Shu, the twenty mounted attendants of my carriage and fast-steed escorts — you executed nearly all of them; my Long-stock cavalry escort still would not suffice for you."
proposals.reason: 隴種 is lineage or stock of Long, not the toponym Longzhong.

proposals.before: The emperor was delighted, gave him ten fine horses, and sent him to seize the Wei south bank, capture Yongfeng Granary, raise five thousand troops, and help take the capital.
proposals.after: The emperor was delighted, gave him ten fine horses, and sent him to seize territory in Weinan, capture Yongfeng Granary, raise five thousand troops, and help take the capital.
proposals.reason: 渭南 is the place Weinan rather than a descriptive Wei south bank.

proposals.before: He was promoted to general of the left guards and awarded five hundred rolls of silk and goods.
proposals.after: He was promoted to grand general of the left commanding army and awarded five hundred rolls of silk and goods.
proposals.reason: Chinese 左領軍大將軍 is Grand General of the Left Commanding Army, not the Left Guards (左衛).

proposals.before: He was transferred to General of the Left Guards and given five hundred rolls of goods.
proposals.after: He was transferred to Grand General of the Left Commanding Army and given five hundred rolls of goods.
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 左領軍 as Left Guards.

proposals.before: His father Rongding served the Sui as military governor of Ming and duke of Chen, posthumously titled Majestic.
proposals.after: His father Rongding served the Sui as military governor of Ming and duke of Chen, posthumously titled Yi (Admirable).
proposals.reason: 諡曰懿 is the posthumous name Yi/Admirable, not Majestic.

proposals.before: As the Emperor's nephew he was early eminent; he entered the Imperial Academy and upon first appointment was made Palace Guard Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Bag.
proposals.after: As the Emperor's nephew he was early eminent; he entered the Imperial Academy and upon first appointment was made Palace Guard Attendant and Equal to the Three Dignitaries.
proposals.reason: Chinese has 儀同三司, not 金紫光祿大夫; the literal line invents the golden-bag rank.

proposals.before: When Prince of Han Liang rebelled, Emperor Yang suspected Kang might join him and sent Li Zixiong at full speed to relieve him of command.
proposals.after: When Liang, Prince of Han, rebelled, Emperor Yang suspected Kang might join him and sent Li Zixiong at full speed to relieve him of command.
proposals.reason: 漢王諒 is Liang, Prince of Han; the idiomatic line fuses title and given name.

proposals.before: Emperor Yang sent Kang to Lingwu to patrol the Great Wall. Learning Gaozu had taken the capital, Kang exclaimed with delight, "My kinsman by marriage is broad-minded and magnanimous — a true prince to restore order."
proposals.after: Emperor Yang sent Kang to Lingwu to patrol the Great Wall. Learning that Gaozu had taken the capital, Kang exclaimed with delight, "The son-in-law of our house is broad-minded and magnanimous — a true prince to restore order."
proposals.reason: Learning Gaozu is ungrammatical, and 吾家婿 is son-in-law of our house.

proposals.before: He received a company of court musicians and treasures beyond reckoning.
proposals.after: He received a troupe of female musicians and treasures beyond reckoning.
proposals.reason: Chinese 女樂 designates female musicians or entertainers; the idiomatic rendering drops that specification.

proposals.before: He also sowed discord among their tribes; the nine yishi chiefs including Yugu'ni under Yuju's division all submitted inward.
proposals.after: He also sowed discord among their tribes; the nine yishi chiefs including Yugu'ni under Yujue's division all submitted inward.
proposals.reason: The same personal name 郁射 is Yujue in the idiomatic English but Yuju in the literal English.

proposals.before: The emperor did not adopt the plan but praised Jing's loyalty and replied graciously: "I entrust all northern affairs to you. As Pacification Commissioner for the North, you leave me with no worry for that frontier."
proposals.after: The emperor did not adopt the plan but praised Jing's loyalty and replied graciously: "I entrust all northern affairs to you. As Ningshuo Commissioner, you leave me with no worry for that frontier."
proposals.reason: 甯朔大使 is the title Ningshuo Commissioner, not a generic northern pacification commissioner.

proposals.before: He died and was posthumously made minister of public works and governor of Jing, posthumously titled An.
proposals.after: He died and was posthumously made minister of public works and prefect of Jingzhou, posthumously titled An.
proposals.reason: 荊州刺史 is prefect of Jingzhou; English Jing collides with the personal name Jing used elsewhere.

proposals.before: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang of Northern Zhou and was enfeoffed duke of Julu.
proposals.after: His grandfather Zhao married Princess Yiyang, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was enfeoffed duke of Julu.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 周文帝義陽公主 identifies the princess as Emperor Wen of Zhou's daughter; the idiomatic line keeps Northern Zhou but drops Emperor Wen.

proposals.before: Dexuan began as a thousand-bull officer in Gaozu's chancellor's office and remained relatively obscure through Taizong's reign. Honoring him as an old minister, Gaozong raised him from vice director of the palace department to censor-in-chief and within a year moved him to vice minister of revenue.
proposals.after: Dexuan began as a qianniu imperial bodyguard in Gaozu's chancellor's office and remained relatively obscure through Taizong's reign. Honoring him as an old minister, Gaozong raised him from vice director of the palace department to censor-in-chief and within a year moved him to vice minister of revenue.
proposals.reason: 千牛 is the qianniu bodyguard post; 'thousand-bull officer' is a calque that obscures the office.

decisions.reason: The source gives Xue Daoheng the Sui office 司隸大夫 and Cui Zujun 起居舍人, not the golden-seal grand-master or household-attendant ranks used in the original English.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 隋司隸大夫薛道衡、起居舍人崔祖浚

decisions.reason: The same two offices are mistranslated in the literal English; 司隸大夫 and 起居舍人 are the capital-inspector grand master and the imperial diarist.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 司隸大夫薛道衡、起居舍人崔祖浚

decisions.reason: The sentence names only 硃鳶 and a 瘴癘地; Annam is an added gloss, and miasmas more faithfully render 瘴癘 than 'southern climes'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 貶為硃鳶主簿，以母老不可居瘴癘地

decisions.reason: 開府儀同三司 is ceremonial equality with the Three Ministers, not the golden-bag grand-master honorific, and 同中書門下三品 is third rank with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 加開府儀同三司、同中書門下三品，知政事

decisions.reason: The literal line likewise replaces 開府儀同三司 with a golden-bag title the Chinese does not give, and misstates 同中書門下三品.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 加開府儀同三司、同中書門下三品

decisions.reason: The Chinese names 崔幹 as the third surname; the original English drops that personal name and treats the ranking as a clan-wide demotion of 'the Cui'.

The idiomatic line already identifies the seven surnames and ten houses by choronym and branch count; expanding it into the ancestral name-list is a shift toward the literal register, not a correction of a false statement.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 凡七姓十家，不得自為昏

decisions.reason: The article in 'a abuse' is ungrammatical; 'an abuse' is the required correction of 世以為敝.
太子詹事 is the supervisor of the heir apparent's household, not the grand master of ceremonies (太常).
The literal English makes the same 太子詹事 / 太常 confusion.
八柱國 are the Eight Pillars of State, hereditary grandees, not 'pillar states'.
The literal quotation repeats the same misreading of 八柱國 as territorial 'pillar states'.

decisions.after: Later, summoned to court, he was granted a seat in the imperial tower but sat without proper decorum; when again seated to receive an imperial message, the emperor in anger said, "When you went to Shu you all but wiped out the twenty mounted guards I gave you — my own cavalry of Long stock would scarcely be enough for you."
decisions.reason: 隴種 is Long stock, not the place Longzhong; the proposed 'Long-stock cavalry' calque is still awkward, so the phrase is recast as 'cavalry of Long stock'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 我隴種車騎，尚不足給公

decisions.after: Later he entered court; granted a seat in the imperial tower, his bearing was not respectful; again seated facing the edict, the Emperor angrily said: "When you entered Shu, the twenty mounted attendants of my carriage and fast-steed escorts — you executed nearly all of them; my cavalry of Long stock still would not suffice for you."
decisions.reason: The literal line has the same Longzhong error; 'Long-stock' is replaced with the more natural 'cavalry of Long stock' for 隴種.
渭南 is the place Weinan; 'Wei south bank' invents a riverbank the source does not name.
左領軍大將軍 is Grand General of the Left Commanding Army, not a general of the Left Guards (左衛).
The literal English likewise renders 左領軍 as Left Guards and omits that the rank is 大將軍.
諡曰懿 is the posthumous name Yi (Admirable), not Majestic.
The appointment is 儀同三司, not 金紫光祿大夫; the golden-bag grand-master rank is invented.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 釋褐千牛備身、儀同三司

decisions.reason: 漢王諒 is Liang, Prince of Han; 'Prince of Han Liang' fuses the title and the given name into one phrase.
吾家婿 is specifically 'son-in-law of our house', and the participle needs a complement ('Learning that Gaozu').
女樂一部 specifies female musicians; 'court musicians' drops the sex of the troupe.
郁射 is Yujue in the idiomatic line and the extracted name; the literal 'Yuju' is an inconsistent romanization of the same person.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 郁射所部鬱孤尼等九俟斤

decisions.reason: 甯朔大使 is the titled office Ningshuo Commissioner, not a generic 'Pacification Commissioner for the North'.
荊州刺史 is prefect of Jingzhou; 'governor of Jing' both misstates the office and collides with the personal name Jing.
周文帝義陽公主 identifies Princess Yiyang as Emperor Wen of Zhou's daughter; the original keeps Northern Zhou but omits Emperor Wen.
千牛 is the qianniu bodyguard post; 'thousand-bull officer' is a misleading calque of the office name.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 德玄始為高祖丞相府千牛

claimRevisions.reason: The accepted repair restores the title-plus-name order Liang, Prince of Han for 漢王諒; the extracted English title had fused them as 'Prince of Han Liang'.
